payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When a verified task produces normal tool artifacts, I want to finish shipping without manual cache moves, so I can return to feature work while unrelated files and failed cleanup remain recoverable.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run normal full verification and prepare pinned build artifacts in a harness task worktree.
2. Approve ship and resume the loop. Cleanup refuses project bytecode, pytest, Ruff, import-linter cache and verified build outputs.
3. Observe that the current ship implementation has already closed the record before cleanup raises. A repeat loop run reports already shipped and leaves the worktree behind.
4. A driver currently has to preserve about twenty generated paths manually, invoke worktree cleanup separately, and commit remaining tracker state. The progress task basicly-8vy4 reproduced this exact failure; later tasks used manual preservation before ship to avoid it.

## Scope

- `.importlinter`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/worktree_contents.py`
- `src/basicly/worktree_preservation.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker.py`
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`
- `tests/test_owned_write_completion.py`
- `tests/test_loop_cleanup_retry.py`
- `tests/test_worktree.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_contents.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_preservation.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_safety.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Design

Keep artifact ownership strict and evidence based. Derive known generated-artifact recognition from the actual producers and pinned build manifest, preserving unknown content, symlinks, tracked changes and all existing checkout identity/lock/unmerged guards. Prefer reversible preservation when ownership does not justify discarding an artifact; never treat every ignored path as disposable. Centralize behavior so ordinary worktree cleanup and loop ship share it. A failed cleanup must leave an open, retryable record; actual criterion confirmation still precedes teardown. Keep completion refusals recoverable and repeated attempts idempotent. Do not touch other sessions or historical worktrees, require force, change permissions, add dependencies or bypass hooks.

## Demonstration

Install the candidate into a disposable consumer, run verification that creates the supported actual tool artifacts, land normally, and ship using ordinary loop commands with no manual cache relocation. Exercise foreign and malformed cache files, symlinks and a cleanup failure: they must preserve data and the open record. Remove only the fixture-owned blocker and retry; assert one clean closure and no live worktree. Keep actual argv, outputs, archive/preservation locations where applicable and elapsed command time in the proof.

payload.description:
## Context

Verified against claude 2.1.231 on 2026-08-13 by probe, with a positive control.

`skills:` in an agent definition is a **documented, typed** frontmatter field: "Skills to
preload into the subagent's context at startup. The full skill content is injected, not only
the description."

It is honoured when the definition is spawned as a subagent - probed: a definition declaring
`skills: [probeskill]`, spawned via the Agent tool and told not to use the Skill tool,
returned the skill's canary token.

**It is not honoured under `claude --agent <name> -p`, which is this repo's dispatch shape.**
Probed twice: same definition, same skill, `NONE` returned, `num_turns 1`. The positive
control loaded the same skill via the Skill tool in the same mode and returned the canary, so
the probe discriminates. Corroborated by the vendor's own `--agent` section, which says the
session takes on the subagent's "system prompt, tool restrictions, and model" - skills are
not in that list.

Consequence today: `.claude/agents/implementer.md`, `decomposer.md`, `validator.md`,
`researcher.md` and `retrospector.md` all declare `skills:` and every one of them gets
nothing from it. The specialist runs without its specialism, and `catalog_lint` enforces a
pairing that has no runtime effect.

This also resolves the open half of `basicly-6vr6` and refutes `agents.py:372`, which calls
the key "deliberately untyped (its shape is the host's to define)". The shape is a documented
list of skill names; the defect is the spawn mode.

## Proposed check

Dispatch through a path that spawns the definition as a subagent (the Python Agent SDK's
`agents={name: AgentDefinition(skills=[...])}`), and assert the preload with a canary: a test
that dispatches a role whose skill contains a unique token and asserts the token reaches the
agent without a `Skill` invocation.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Project the agents (`basicly agents-build`), leaving `implementer.md` declaring
  `skills: [python-guidelines, repair-in-place]`.
- Dispatch it the way the engine does: `claude --agent implementer -p "<prompt>"`, with the
  prompt asking for a token that appears only inside one of those skill bodies.
- Observed: `NONE`, `num_turns 1` - probed twice on claude 2.1.231, 2026-08-13. The positive
  control loaded the same skill through the Skill tool in the same mode and returned the
  canary, so the probe discriminates between "absent" and "wrong probe".
- Expected: the agent holds the skill body without invoking the Skill tool.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/roles.py`
- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_roles.py`
- `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

The finding stands on its own - skills: is inert under claude --agent -p - and xjd2 builds on it.

OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 - the fix is PROMPT INJECTION, not the Agent SDK. Measured before deciding: the largest role's declared skills are 3261 tokens (implementer: python-guidelines + repair-in-place) against a lane costing 8-11M, so injecting the bodies costs about 0.03% of a lane. The SDK route was rejected on two grounds: it is claude-only in a harness that advertises three families, and it is a new runtime dependency every basicly install consumer inherits, whose behaviour tracks the CLI product's release cadence rather than a pinned library's (basicly-ctdz's criterion). Named failure mode to measure, not assume: skills: injects at startup ahead of the first turn while a prompt prefix arrives as user text, so ADHERENCE may differ even though the content is identical - the canary test must assert the content arrives, and a follow-up should measure whether it is followed.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When install runs over an existing `.claude/settings.json` with uncommitted or untracked content, a `.basicly-bak` copy equal to the old bytes exists afterwards, and install prints its path.
- When the file is malformed JSON, install exits non-zero, names the file and the parse position, and writes nothing.
- When the file carries a user-authored key, a user hook and `includeCoAuthoredBy: false`, afterwards the key and hook are unchanged, `attribution` holds the equivalent value, and `includeCoAuthoredBy` is gone.
- When `settings.local.json` carries an absolute path or a blanket allow, install lists the finding and the file's bytes are unchanged.
- When `--dry-run` runs, it prints the key-level summary and no file changes.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When `basicly install` runs in a repo that already has `.claude/settings.json` (or `settings.local.json`), I want to merge the baseline into it by a written rule and keep a restorable copy of the old file, so I can install into an existing repo without losing or silently changing its settings.

## Context

Today `permissions-build` and `hooks-build` merge additively into `.claude/settings.json` (`merge_permission_deny`, `merge_agent_hooks` in `src/basicly/claude_settings.py`) and keep no copy. The `.basicly-bak` backups cover scaffold files and untracked projected files only (`cli.py` `SCAFFOLD_BACKUP_SUFFIX`, `projection.back_up_unrecognised`). A malformed settings file is not refused by name: probed 2026-09-25 in a scratch repo, `sync_permission_deny` raises `JSONDecodeError` on a trailing comma, and `cmd_permissions_build` has no handler for it.

## Merge rule, per key

- Managed lists (`permissions.deny`, `permissions.ask`): union, existing entries kept, order kept.
- Managed hooks: replaced by script identity, as today; a user hook on the same event stays.
- `permissions.allow`: kept. Install reports an entry that makes a managed rule moot (a blanket `Bash`, `Edit` or `Write`; an allow that equals a managed `ask` entry) and does not delete it.
- Deprecated keys (`includeCoAuthoredBy`): migrated to `attribution` with the same meaning, and the old key removed.
- Any key basicly does not own: left byte-for-byte as it was.
- `settings.local.json`: never written. Install lists findings only: absolute paths, user or host names, broad allows (`Bash(git *)`, `Bash(uv run *)`, `Bash(python3 -)`), and allows that override a managed `ask`.

## Backup

Before the first write that changes an existing `.claude/settings.json`, install writes `.claude/settings.json.basicly-bak`, unless the file is tracked and has no uncommitted change (git holds that copy). Install prints the backup path and a key-level summary of what changed. `--dry-run` prints the same summary and writes nothing.
payload.requirements:
- One merge function owns the rule. `permissions-build`, `hooks-build` and install call it; none copies it.
- A regression test covers each per-key rule and the malformed-file refusal.
payload.title: Merge the baseline into an existing Claude settings file by rule and keep a restorable copy

payload.description:
When a catalog source carries a table whose delimiter row is unpadded while its cells are padded, I want the authoring gate to refuse it, so I can stop shipping markdown that fails a consumer's default lint.

Found by the terminal canary as term-fawxo, blocking their upgrade commit on 62 errors after they cleared their own 31. Reproduced here: this repository's projections produce 20 MD060 errors under a consumer config with no basicly config present, against a ragged table as the positive control.

All 20 are style compact and the cause is one shape. A table writes a padded header and padded cells while leaving the delimiter row bare - pipe dash dash dash pipe - so markdownlint infers compact from the delimiter and then objects to every padded cell. The table is internally inconsistent, which is what the rule exists to catch.

basicly-jaz4 disabled MD060 here for a reason that does not govern this: it named an ALIGNED table, where editing one cell forces a hand re-pad of every other pipe and fix will not do it. None of these are aligned. The remedy is to pad the delimiter row, two characters per column, once.
payload.requirements: the fix is in the catalog sources rather than the projector, so the projector never rewrites authored prose. Any later normaliser splits on unescaped pipes only, because an escaped pipe in a table documenting the pipe operator splits into a phantom column and the damage reads as padding. basicly-jaz4 is annotated rather than left reading as blanket cover.
payload.title: pad the delimiter rows and gate the rule that caught them

payload.description:
## Context

The owner requires repository-owned onboarding for persistent agent memory.
One person configures the repository and commits all required shared setup.
Other machines receive the instructions, skills and bootstrap through clone or pull.
Agents must establish tracker context before implementation. Missing memory must stop work.
Related feature: basicly-gtb19bg.43.

## Scope

Detect missing machine setup from committed repository guidance and executable startup paths.
Configure the existing tracker without repeating repository migration.
Cover standalone and harness entrypoints. Preserve unrelated settings and frozen history.
Stop with a named remedy when prerequisites, permissions or vault access prevent setup.
Do not claim arbitrary third-party agents are blocked without an actual enforcement path.

## Confirmation Plan

Use public installer and agent-start regressions with fresh homes and repository copies.
Exercise clone, pull introduction, successful bootstrap, repeated startup and unavailable context.
Run affected standalone, agent installation, hook and consumer checks.
Keep existing gates and original concurrency tests unchanged.

payload.description:
## Problem

`basicly` projects its Claude hooks into every consumer's `.claude/settings.json` with a **relative**
script path, so each one fails whenever the agent's working directory is not the repo root.

`claude_settings._agent_hook_command` renders `uv run python <hooks_relpath>/<script>`, and its
docstring justifies the shape by mirroring the pre-commit entries. That precedent does not transfer:
a pre-commit hook always runs from the repo root, while a Claude Code hook handler runs in the
**current** directory. That is the exact fact `basicly-dukb` established from the vendor docs, and
`.basicly/core/kit/install_hook.py` already ships the correct form for the tier-injection hook —
`uv run --no-project --no-python-downloads python "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/..."`, where the host
substitutes the placeholder as a plain string before any shell sees it, so it also works under
PowerShell.

So the repo fixed this for the kit and left its own two projected hooks — `tool-usage` (PostToolUse)
and `protect-generated` (PreToolUse) — on the broken form. Observed live in this repo: a `cd` into a
directory outside the root made the PostToolUse hook fail with
`can't open file '<other-dir><redacted:posix-absolute-path>': [Errno 2] No such file or
directory`. The PreToolUse case is worse in kind: `protect-generated` is a guard, and a guard that
cannot start is not protecting anything.

This has been survivable here only because an operator carried the workaround as habit ("never use a
bare `cd`"). A consumer inherits the broken hook and none of the habit.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
uv run python -c "
from basicly import claude_settings
from basicly.hooks import HookSpec
print(claude_settings._agent_hook_command(
    HookSpec(id='tool-usage', script='tool-usage.py', stage='post-tool-use'),
    '.basicly/core/hooks'))
"
```

Observed - `uv run python '.basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py'`, a relative path. Then, from any
directory other than the repo root, that command cannot find its script. Expected - the same
`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`-qualified form the kit installer already uses, so the hook resolves from any
working directory and still contains no machine-specific absolute path.

Both hook scripts are stdlib-only (no `basicly` import), so `--no-project` is safe for them, matching
the kit.

## Scope

- src/basicly/claude_settings.py
- tests/test_claude_settings.py

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given basicly projects its managed Claude hooks into a repo when the agent's working directory is
  not the repo root then each hook still resolves and runs, the projected command contains no
  machine-specific absolute path, and re-running the projection over the previous relative-path form
  replaces it rather than leaving both
payload.title: Projected claude hooks use a relative script path so they break outside the repo root

payload.description:
## Context

Owner verdict 2026-08-21 on the shipped Mode A page: *"visibility is zero. I do not see what features are being implemented, the visualization of the loop and where the current implementation is, in which state, I do not see the backlog, and I have no idea how to read any of it."*

The layout is a separate defect. This one is the data behind it. Measured on a snapshot from this repository:

```text
units      233 entries, fields: id, priority, status, title, type
           phase  = null on 233 of 233
           ready  = 0   on 233 of 233
lanes      ABSENT
session    ABSENT
asks       1 entry, fields: issue, kind, requested_at, subject, wait_id
repo       name only
```

So the loop position of every open unit is unknowable, the ready set is unknowable, the grant and its budget are unknowable, and an ask carries no question and no waiting time. A renderer cannot draw what the producer never sent.

## Why the producer is right to omit them, and what that means

`board_sections.units` states it: *"`phase` has the same authority problem `LaneFacts` documents, and `ready` is the tracker own derivation over a status vocabulary and the whole edge population... both stay absent until a caller supplies them."* That is the layer rule of architecture 34.1 - the layer above supplies the fact the layer below cannot honestly derive - and it must not be broken by giving `board_sections` a second spelling of `loop_state.derive_phase`.

**So the fix is the caller, never the section.** `build_document` takes the derivations as arguments, exactly as it already takes the lane and lock facts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the caller supplies a phase per record, EACH units row SHALL carry it, and the value SHALL come from `loop_state.derive_phase` rather than from a second derivation.
- WHEN the caller supplies the ready set, EACH units row SHALL carry `ready`, and `backlog` SHALL carry `ready` and `blocked`.
- WHEN a grant is live, `session` SHALL carry `grant_level`, `token_budget` and `spent_tokens`.
- WHEN a wait is pending, ITS asks row SHALL carry `question` and `waiting_s`.
- WHEN the repository is read, `repo` SHALL carry `branch`, `head` and `dirty`.
- WHERE a fact cannot be derived, THE SECTION SHALL stay absent rather than carry a zero, and a test SHALL prove the absence renders as absent.
- WHEN `basicly board validate` runs over the emitted document, IT SHALL report ok with no new violation.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_snapshot.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_board_snapshot.py`
- `tests/test_board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_board_usage.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `150000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>` then read the emitted snapshot and assert the first units row carries a real phase name, `backlog.ready` is positive, and `session.token_budget` is present under a live grant.
payload.title: the board omits the fields a wall board is read for so every panel is empty or a count

payload.description:
## Context

Step 2 of the cutover in `docs/design/work-tracker.md` §5. Step 1 ran 2026-08-07
(commit `b97a653`): the ledger now holds 3775 events over 643 records, imported with
provenance EXTRACTED, and `fsck` reports zero errors.

Step 2 is shadow mode - the owned tracker answers the same queries read-only and a
differential asserts identical verdicts for phase derivation, ready set and gate status.
Every piece of machinery exists and none of it is wired to anything real. Measured
2026-08-07: `differential.run_differential` and `differential.ReferenceSource` are
constructed in `tests/test_kit_tracker_differential.py` only. No engine module, CLI
command or script builds a source from the live tracker, so the differential has never
been run against this repo.

## The reference must be live, not a re-import

§5.1 records why, and the kit already enforces it: `import` upstream is upsert-only and
cannot express deletion, so comparing two derivatives of one lossy snapshot agrees with
itself and proves nothing. `ReferenceSource` carries `snapshot=None` for a live source
and `audit_reference` perturbs the owned event set to catch a source that is secretly a
derivative - a source that changes its answer when the ledger is perturbed is refused.
So the work is a `views` callable that reads the live `br` and ignores its argument
entirely.

Report `clean` and `conclusive` separately, as the kit already does. A refused reference
still runs the comparison, and the report must say in the same breath that the agreement
proves nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the imported ledger and a reference source built from the live br when the shadow differential runs then it reports clean and conclusive separately and a perturbed ledger makes the audit refuse the source rather than reporting a clean comparison

## Scope

- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_br_seam.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`

payload.value:
## Trigger

When a prefix remap on import rewrites only the id field and leaves the same prefix inside title, description, notes, close_reason and nested dependency edges, I want the migration runbook to name every touched field and the safe rewrite method, so I can stop an import from silently corrupting prose.

## Context

A consumer whose source prefix carries a hyphen must rewrite it before importing, and nothing tells them the prefix appears outside the id field. In the burndown-chart export it appeared in id, title, description, notes and close_reason, and dependency edges are nested rather than top level. payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
uv run python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from basicly import decompose
print(decompose.scope_read_cost(Path('.'), ['src/basicly/cli.py']))"
rg -n "read only the ranges you need" .basicly/core/fragments/
```

Observed - a scope naming `cli.py` costs its whole 91,839 characters, while the harness's own always-on guidance tells the agent not to read it that way. Expected - the estimate reflects the material a lane must reason over.

## Context

The ceiling half of `basicly-3w44` is closed. This is the measure half, and it is the one that unblocks chunking.

`decompose.scope_read_cost` is "tokenized size of the existing files matching the declared scope globs" - the whole of every named file. The band compares that against a budget of "material to reason over" (`config.py`). Those are the same quantity only if a lane reads every line of every file it names, and the repo's own `tool-usage` fragment forbids exactly that: "find files by name, localize with focused search, read only the ranges you need".

**Measured over 23 real headless lane transcripts** (off-repo, under the agent's own project directory, all `entrypoint: sdk-cli`):

| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Read` calls that are ranged | 75% |
| median fraction of a read file actually read | 0.207 |
| same, for files over 1500 lines | 0.078 |
| same, for `cli.py` | 0.027 |
| read material falling inside the declared scope | 37% |
| Bash output tokens vs Read output tokens | 443,860 vs 390,908 |
| estimate over measured, across 17 lanes with a declared scope | 0.17x to 4.65x |
| least-squares fit | `measured = 13464 + 1.075 x scope_read_cost` |
| measured material range (median) | 6k-99k (17k) |

Two consequences. The seed factors (3.0/2.0/1.5) are about **3x the empirical slope**, and there is a **~13.5k ambient term the formula has no slot for** - Bash output alone exceeds Read output and is unmodelled. And measured material is the same order as the original 64000 ceiling, which means the ceiling was roughly right and the **measure** is the defect. The 112000 raised by 3w44 (a) is therefore a compensating adjustment for a biased estimator, not a settled value; when the estimator is fixed the ceiling should come back down, and 3w44's gate is formula-relative so it will demand that on its own.

**Sub-file scope is dead on arrival.** Proven by running the real functions, not by reasoning: `globs_overlap('cli.py','cli.py:100-200')` is `False`, `scope_read_cost` of a ranged glob is `0`, and `merge._scope_covers` misses every diff path. Eleven consumers treat a scope glob as a set of paths with no filesystem access - grouping (`decompose.py:298`), collapsing paths (`:358`), merge coupling (`merge.py:749/797/831/870`), the loop scope-collision gate (`loop.py:798`), supervise found-info folding (`supervise.py:668/724`). Only the sizing chain treats it as a quantity. So changing the glob **grammar** breaks eleven consumers and would silently parallelize two lanes on one file while writing wrong permanent coupling edges; changing only the **function applied to globs**, or adding a second field, is safe.

**Telemetry is absent in-repo.** The `tool-usage` hook matches `Bash|Skill` only (`.basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py:3`) - 508 entries, zero file paths. `RunRecord` has no read or context field. Runner stdout is parsed in-process and discarded (`runner.py:226`). `decompose.py:702-706` already says so.

**Order matters.** Record `context_tokens` on `RunRecord` first: one additive field, gates nothing, and it is what both this bead and the ceiling need. Fitting a formula before the field exists is how the 216x build factor happened.

The counter-argument to the leading candidate, stated so it is not rediscovered: a per-file cap alone unblocks all six false refusals **but drops `basicly-kjc5.44` - one of the two lanes that actually failed, at 99,432 measured tokens - to 0.24x**, trading a visible false refusal for an invisible false admission of the exact lane that got SIGTERMed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a dispatched lane when it completes then the run record carries the context it actually consumed so the estimator can be fitted to a measurement rather than a proxy
- Given a small change to a large file when its scope is sized then the estimate is not the whole file and decompose does not refuse it for size alone
- Given the scope globs when the measure changes then grouping scope-overlap collision detection and merge coupling attribution behave exactly as before and a test proves each
- Given the recorded lane outcomes when the new estimator is applied then no lane that completed is refused and no lane that failed for size is admitted

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `tests/test_decompose.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `CHANGELOG.md`
- `docs/design/factory-design.md`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`

Widened at build time. `runner.py` is the only dispatch site that can write `context_tokens`, `config.py` carries the ceiling the estimator derives, and `3w44`'s gate is formula-relative so it demands that re-derivation on its own.
payload.title: Scope read cost sizes whole files so a small change to a large module cannot be chunked

payload.description:
Measured 2026-08-09 in base @ 5132143, while decomposing basicly-u2hl.54.

ROLE_BY_PHASE (roles.py:63) has seven entries and reviewer is not among them:

  classify -> decider          build -> implementer      retrospective -> retrospector
  decompose -> decomposer      validate -> validator     ship -> curator
                               repair -> implementer

`.claude/agents/reviewer.md` and `.agents/agents/reviewer.md` both exist and are projected,
and the reviewer agent's own description says it is 'invoked by the engine at VALIDATE, once
per lens, alongside the validator'. But VALIDATE maps to validator alone, so even after
basicly-u2hl.54 lands and VALIDATE becomes a real phase, nothing can reach reviewer.

The comment at roles.py:55-62 explains that VALIDATE, REPAIR and RETROSPECTIVE are recorded
without phases on purpose. It does not cover reviewer, which has no phase to be waiting for.

Two honest resolutions, and this bead is to pick one rather than to assume:

1. VALIDATE dispatches more than one role - validator plus one reviewer per lens - in which
   case ROLE_BY_PHASE is the wrong shape, because it is phase -> one role. That is a design
   change, and it should be settled against factory-loop.md section 6 rather than here.
2. reviewer is not an engine-dispatched role at all and the agent should be deleted or
   re-described, because an agent nothing routes to is context load with no reach - the same
   argument that just moved 15 tool skills to user-invoked (basicly-a3ab.12).

Do not resolve this by adding 'validate' -> 'reviewer' to the map. That would displace
validator, which basicly-u2hl.54.3 is being built to dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The repo shall either route reviewer from a named phase through `roles.resolve_role`, or
  carry no projected reviewer agent, and a test shall assert that every projected agent file
  under the loop-role set is reachable from `ROLE_BY_PHASE`.
- Where the answer is that VALIDATE fans out to several roles, the decision shall be recorded
  in `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md` before `ROLE_BY_PHASE` changes shape.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/roles.py`
- `.basicly/core/agents/`
- `tests/test_roles.py`
- `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `rg -n 'ROLE_BY_PHASE' -A 10 src/basicly/roles.py` - seven entries, no reviewer.
2. `ls .claude/agents/reviewer.md` - the agent exists and is projected.
3. There is no phase string for which `roles.role_for_phase` returns 'reviewer'.
payload.title: Map the reviewer role to a phase or delete the agent

payload.description:
## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22 as part of "we need improvements all over the board". The wall shows fourteen of one hundred and eighty seven ready units and prints `NEXT UP — +173 MORE READY`.

## The cap is fixed to the smallest supported wall

`board_regions.py:83-97` declares `READY_SLOTS_WIDE = 14` and `READY_SLOTS = 8`, and its own comment states the arithmetic: *14 rows of 24.1px under an 18.2px heading is what fits ... against 26 at 1920x1080*, and *both figures are the shortest wall this layout claims, not the roomiest*.

So on a 1920x1080 screen the region draws 14 rows where 26 fit. Measured on a probe render at 1920x1080: exactly 14 `<tr>` elements. Roughly half the available height is left blank, by construction rather than by overflow.

Row geometry, measured from `board_page.html.j2:412-416`: font-size 17px, line-height 1.3, padding 1px 0, giving 24.1px per row under an 18.2px heading.

## Why a fixed cap was right and is not now

A fixed cap cannot overflow, and the overflow instrument (`.scripts/check_render_overflow.py`) exists because four board pages shipped clipped. Choosing the smallest wall was the safe answer before that instrument existed. It now exists, so a fit computed from the viewport can be **measured** at each width the layout claims rather than assumed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the wall renders at a given viewport height, THE NUMBER OF ROWS DRAWN SHALL be derived from that height and the measured row geometry, not from a constant.
- WHEN the derived count exceeds what fits, THE RENDER SHALL NOT clip, and `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` SHALL report neither overflow nor overlap at every width the layout claims.
- WHEN rows are omitted, THE HEADING SHALL still state how many, as it does now.
- WHERE the viewport is unknown to the producer, THE FIT SHALL be resolved where the viewport is known rather than guessed at build time.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: `basicly-v8jwf0`
- demonstration: Render at 1440x900, 1600x1200 and 1920x1080, count the rows drawn at each, and run `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` at each width reading both the overflow line and the overlap line.

payload.description:
## Context

Three instances on 2026-08-21, in three different code paths, all one shape: a gate refused, and what reached the operator named no gate.

```text
the salvage commit was rejected: protect-generated-commit...........Passed
routed: basicly-s07cgc -> error - routing failed: command failed (1): git commit -m ...
routed: basicly-co64   -> error - routing failed: command failed (1): git commit -m ...
```

The first prints a **passing** hook line as the rejection reason. The other two print the argv and the exit code and nothing else. In every case the real cause was one named check inside the captured output: markdownlint refusing a lane`s own gitignored scratch note in the first, `release-notes` naming the exact missing `changelog.d/<id>.<category>.md` in the other two.

## Why this costs more than it looks

Each one cost a diagnosis that the output already contained. The salvage case is worse than silence: a reader who trusts the line goes and looks at `protect-generated-commit`, which passed.

The repo already knows this class. `basicly-e84` closed on *"verify from explicit pass/fail lines not truncated output"*, and `basicly-lkzq` records that a hand-picked subset of checks reads exactly like the gate. This is the same rule turned inward: the engine`s own error text is doing to an operator what a truncated tail does to an agent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a git command the engine runs fails because a hook refused, THE ENGINE SHALL name the failing check and its reported reason rather than the argv and the exit code.
- WHEN the captured output holds an explicit failure line, THE MESSAGE SHALL carry that line and SHALL NOT carry a passing line.
- WHEN no failure line can be identified, THE MESSAGE SHALL say so and name where the full output was written, so the fallback is honest rather than misleading.
- WHERE a lane close trips `release-notes`, THE MESSAGE SHALL carry the fix the gate already prints.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Drive a close whose `release-notes` gate refuses and read the failure name the check itself printed, against a control close that succeeds and prints no such line.

[scope correction 2026-08-22] The landing gate bounced this lane to rework for changing eleven files outside its declared scope. The record was wrong, not the work, and the lane said so itself in its own commit body before the gate did: the declared scope named loop.py, supervise.py, verify.py and tests/test_loop.py, and the producers of an opaque git failure are checkout.py, commit.py and merge.py. checkout.run read stderr-or-stdout, where stdout holds the whole pre-commit report and stderr holds a uv warning on every run in this tree; commit.salvage quoted the last line of the hook chain, which belongs to whichever hook ran last - here a hook that had PASSED. Neither is reachable from the declared four.

The scope is now what the lane built. Re-dispatching would have spent about thirty million tokens rebuilding correct work.

VERIFIED BEFORE CORRECTING, not assumed: uv run basicly verify --mode full on harness/basicly-fi1i7z fails on exactly one check, release-notes, and the gate itself says why - changelog.d/basicly-03ykuf.fixed.md is on the base branch and absent here, so the tree is BEHIND rather than in debt, and the remedy is a rebase. Every other check passes, test-naming included, with the new module carrying its test file.

THE REAL COLLISION IS THREE FILES, not eleven: .importlinter, docs/architecture/architecture.md and docs/plan/implementation-plan.md, all also declared by basicly-rn0o.6. The other eight are this lane's alone. A blocks edge now serializes this behind rn0o.6, which claimed that ground first, so it rebases onto a landed rn0o.6 rather than racing it. Note the implementation plan conflicts on essentially every merge and its documented resolution is --ours followed by docs_claims.py --fix.

Also worth keeping: the lane refuted its own first design against real output rather than shipping it - a tail of the hook block was the first cut, and pre-commit-script wraps the whole verify suite so its block ends on the list of checks it ran, not on the reason.

payload.description:
## Context

Parent: basicly-lc2bd3v. The owner: *"be able to easily start, stop work"*.

Nothing on the board starts work. `board_asks.pending` builds one action row per implementable *offer*, and a ready record has no ask - so the 234 records the board says are ready carry no way to begin any of them.

## The verb

`basicly loop supervise <id> --max-passes 1 --detach`, not `loop run`: a killed first run cannot be re-dispatched by `loop run`, because `loop run` dispatches once at provisioning. The board must not offer a verb whose second press does nothing.

## No confirm code, and the reason

`checkpoint-approve` carries one because a checkpoint is the human gate the anti-autopilot rule protects; a board that read the minted code and offered a one-click approve would be relaying the code to itself. Starting a lane is not a gate. It is spend, and spend is bounded by the grant the engine already enforces.

So the guard here is a different one: the action is offered only for a record that is **ready and unclaimed**, so a press cannot start a second lane on work already in flight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a record is ready and no lane holds it, THE BOARD SHALL offer to start it, on that record`s own row.
- WHERE a record is already claimed or already has a lane, THE BOARD SHALL NOT offer to start it.
- THE PRINTED COMMAND SHALL be built through the action`s own `build`, so the line a reader copies cannot diverge from the argv the button runs.
- WHEN the action returns, THE BOARD SHALL show the CLI`s own exit status and output rather than a generic success.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_asks.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_asks.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: press start on a ready record and watch a worktree appear

The tests pass because they assert the argv's shape, never that the argv starts anything.

And the deeper finding, which is why the lane could not have got this right: the CLI has no verb that starts ONE ready leaf record detached. 'loop run <id>' is the single-record verb but is synchronous with no --detach, and board_actions.TIMEOUT_S is 300s against a lane that runs for twenty minutes. payload.description:
## Trigger

When two stores hold one record's acceptance criteria and they say different things, I want each conflict read and resolved by a person, so I can collapse them to one store without silently losing what the other held.

## Requirements

R1. No criterion is lost when the two stores collapse to one.
R2. A resolution is made by reading both stores, never by a rule that prefers one.
R3. A reader can tell a reconciled record from an untouched one.
R4. The count of remaining conflicts is visible and falls to zero.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the reconciliation is complete, then no open record holds a `## Acceptance Criteria` heading whose content differs from its `acceptance_criteria` field. [check: `tests/test_tracker_migrate.py` over a fixture of the conflicting shapes]
- When a record is reconciled, then the resulting field holds every distinct criterion that either store held. [check: the reconciliation appends one update event per record and the diff is reviewable]
- When a conflict cannot be resolved from the two stores alone, then the record is left untouched and named in the closing comment. [check: the closing comment]
- When the reconciliation runs, then it edits no line of the log that already exists. [check: `git diff` over `.basicly/ledger/`]

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly tracker list --status open` folded against the two stores, showing zero remaining conflicts

## Scope

Measured 2026-09-13 over 9,427 events: **202 records carry both stores and 94 of them disagree** under a normalised comparison of the heading entries against the field. On `basicly-17nu` the heading reads `todo` while the field holds real criteria. Some of the 94 are formatting near-misses that a comparison cannot separate from real conflicts, which is exactly why this is read rather than scripted.

Only the open subset must be resolved before the gate can bind; the closed ones are evidence and may be left.

## Design notes

Architecture D-50. **A script is refused for this record.** Picking a store loses the other's content, and a prior scripted bulk edit in this repository turned 23 test failures into 80. Ninety-four records is an afternoon of reading.

payload.description:
Every push to main triggers CI (and in consumer repos like <redacted:private-consumer-repo>, a long verify build), but the harness loop currently produces multiple .beads/issues.jsonl-only commits per track (claim, loop-state, close after teardown). Investigate WHY tracker commits were separated from work commits (suspected: worktree provisioning syncs base jsonl and committing on both sides makes the landing rebase conflict - see beads-tracker-vs-loop-worktrees memory and basicly-djt). Then judge and decide the optimal fix, e.g.: fold the close into the last work commit (close bead before the resolving commit), batch pushes until the closing commit lands, and/or paths-ignore .beads/** in CI workflows (authoring + the consumer CI template). br is the essential tracker the harness builds on, so the chosen discipline must be conflict-free with worktrees and documented.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Root cause for the separated tracker commits is documented on this issue with evidence from code/history. A decision comment records the chosen design and rejected alternatives. Implementation lands: workflow/CI changes (including the consumer CI template if applicable) and/or loop commit-discipline changes so tracker-only pushes stop triggering full builds and tracker state stays conflict-free with worktree landings. Agent instructions/skills (tool-br, harness-loop, fragments) updated to the new discipline. Full gate suite passes.
payload.title: Tracker-only commits trigger pointless builds - investigate and fix commit discipline

payload.text: [harness-policy] checkpoint=classify approved

INVESTIGATION (root cause, with evidence): tracker commits are separated from work commits structurally, not accidentally. (1) worktree provisioning copies the BASE WORKING-TREE issues.jsonl into the new worktree (worktree.py create, basicly-djt fix 32dc562) purely so the beads-commit-msg hook recognizes freshly filed ids; (2) merge.py _assert_base_ready requires a CLEAN base checkout at landing, so any base-side tracker mutation (claim, work type, checkpoint approvals - all recorded via br from base) must be committed before the landing advance; (3) the br daemon rewrites the full jsonl export in every checkout, so a harness branch that also commits issues.jsonl guarantees a rebase conflict at merge_worktree step 1 - br sync --merge (reconcile_beads) only runs AFTER a successful merge and cannot rescue the rebase; (4) the close cannot ride the last work commit because loop._on_ship closes the issue AFTER the merge commit exists (phase order: land at build->verify, then verify gate on base, then ship checkpoint, then close). Folding the close into a work commit is therefore impossible in the current two-checkout model; the tool-br rule (close folded into the resolving commit) applies only to non-loop base-checkout work.

DECISION: the pointless builds are a CI-trigger problem, not a commit-count problem - GitHub runs the workflows per push to main regardless of content, and the expensive job is the 3-OS quality-gates matrix (and in consumer repos like <redacted:private-consumer-repo>, the scaffolded basicly-gates workflow / their own verify build). Chosen fix: (a) add paths-ignore .beads/** to the push and pull_request triggers of basicly.yml and quality-gates.yml, and to the CONSUMER_CI_WORKFLOW template so new consumer installs get it; (b) keep tracker commits separate (structural, see investigation) but cut them to exactly two per track via skill discipline: ONE pre-provisioning chore(beads) commit folding claim+work-type+classify approval, and ONE closing commit after ship; (c) push discipline: push once per track after the closing commit, never push tracker-only commits alone. Trade-off accepted: a tracker-only push skips CI commit-message validation for those commits; the local commit-msg hooks are the deterministic floor and already validated them. REJECTED (for now): engine redesign folding the close into the merge commit (git merge --no-commit + stage jsonl) - it requires reordering the loop so landing happens AFTER verify+ship approval (today code lands on main BEFORE the ship checkpoint), would also remove the duplicate base re-verify, but changes governance and feature fan-in semantics; filed separately as a design bead. NOTE for existing consumers: install never overwrites the scaffolded CI workflow, so <redacted:private-consumer-repo> must add paths-ignore .beads/** to its own workflow manually.

payload.description:
When a consumer lints their repository with default markdownlint rules, I want the markdown basicly generated into it to pass, so I can stop shipping output that fails a gate we also ship.

Found by the terminal canary after a v0.14.1 install, filed there as term-fawxo, and blocking their commit. Reproduced here, which is the part that matters: copying this repository's own .claude and .agents projections plus AGENTS.md into a directory carrying a consumer-shaped markdownlint config produces 20 MD060 table-column-style errors. The canary sees 62 because their projection set is larger.

This repository passes only because .markdownlint-cli2.yaml disables MD060 for itself, with a recorded reason under basicly-jaz4: the rule fires when one cell of an aligned table is edited without re-padding, and --fix will not re-pad. That reason is about hand-edited markdown. It was never shipped, so a consumer whose config says default true gets the rule and our output fails it.

The standard this misses is our own. The same config file says a violation in a projected file means a template or catalog source regressed, fix it there and rebuild. The generator is emitting markdown that is not lint-clean and the rule was turned off rather than the output fixed.

The canary also reports 24 MD022 and MD032 errors inside the Commit delta auto-generated section that basicly release writes. That half does NOT reproduce here: this repository's own CHANGELOG.md passes the same consumer config with exit 0, so their 24 need their file to diagnose and are not confirmed as ours.

The first probe I ran reported zero and was wrong: markdownlint merges the repository's own config even under --config, so the rule was disabled in my own measurement. A deliberately ragged table as a positive control did not fire either, which is what exposed it. The numbers above are from a directory that carries no basicly config.
payload.requirements: the fix is at the source or the projector rather than by disabling a rule in the consumer's config, because the consumer's lint config is theirs and a rule we silence for ourselves is not a rule we may silence for them. Whatever is chosen, the scoping advice the install prints must name the same paths as the fix.
payload.title: our generated markdown fails a rule we disabled only for ourselves

payload.text:
The CHANGELOG half is settled and is not ours. Grepping the whole tree for 'Commit delta' returns CHANGELOG.md and the ledger only - no source file, no script, no workflow - against a positive control that the string does exist in CHANGELOG.md. Stronger, because absent today is not absent ever: git log --all -S over src, .scripts and any .py returns nothing, against a control of 4 commits when the same search is scoped to CHANGELOG.md. This repository's one such section was written by a human commit, b0bf6daf, and carries the blank line. So basicly release has never emitted that heading and the canary's 12 sections came from something else; a hand fix there stays fixed. Bound: only this repository was searched.

The canary's escaped-pipe finding is a requirement on any projector fix, recorded before the work starts. Their first re-padding attempt refused to write because a cell containing an escaped pipe, in a table documenting the pipe operator, split into a phantom extra column and would have added an empty cell to every row. Split on unescaped pipes only, (?<!\\)\|. A naive split silently widens the table and the damage reads as padding, which is the shape that passes review.

Their verification standard is the one to hold a fix to: refuse to write unless the parsed cell text is identical, then confirm at the diff level that the removed and added lines are byte-identical after squashing spaces, dashes and colons. Two paths sharing no step.

[measured 2026-10-29] MD060 is on again and our generated AGENTS.md plus 26 SKILL.md files show 0 MD060 findings under default rules. The same run finds 458 MD013/line-length findings and 1 MD041, and MD013 is also disabled only for this repository (.markdownlint-cli2.yaml). Kept open for MD013.

## Trigger
The Anthropic prompting audit (2026-09-12) read `.basicly/core/fragments/security/secure-coding.fragment.yaml` and found four of five bullets state a prohibition with no reason and no alternative.

## Problem
Our own `catalog-authoring` skill requires every prohibition to carry a one-clause rationale and the alternative to take instead. The security fragment breaks that rule in four places, so the rule does not generalise past its literal case.

## Constraint

## Context

Found by the lane-C survey 2026-08-14. The largest item in the backlog and the last in its chain.

After the owned extractions land, the command-line module still cannot be named without the word and. It is the projection and distribution command surface, lines 125 to 1930, and an interactive factory operations console.

```text
loop preflight printing     cli.py:2700-3070
session rendering           cli.py:3441-3560
decisions, answer, kill     cli.py:3561-3823
                            about 1,160 lines
parser wiring               cli.py:4048-4910, about 860 lines
```

The module is 4,911 lines and 51,691 tokens, frozen at 54,336 against a 4,000 cap.

## The seam is a responsibility, not a metric

The loop console has its own state, its own vocabulary and its own test files. The layering contract is exhaustive with the command-line module alone at the top tier, so the new module needs a declared tier between it and the supervisor. It imports the supervisor, the loop, the decisions module and the policy module, and only the command-line module imports it.

## The ratchet arithmetic

The command-line module is frozen on size and not on prose share, so it has prose headroom below the cap. The loop console is printer-heavy code, so the extraction raises the remainder's prose share. Measure both before choosing the exact cut. Record the shrink through the delta mechanism, never by editing the frozen line.

## Acceptance

- When a loop subcommand is invoked, then its handler resolves from a dedicated console module placed in its own declared tier.
- When the command-line module is read after the change, then it retains parser registration only for those commands.
- When any loop command runs, then its output is byte-identical to today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- a new module
- `.importlinter`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py` and its siblings

## Depends on

The supervisor pass extraction, the install lifecycle extraction, and the structured escalation routes. All three move code out of the same file.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -q` and a diff of `uv run basicly loop status` output against the pre-split output.

payload.description:
## Context

Found by `basicly-06pvsc`, and the second half is the interesting defect rather than the stale number.

`.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`'s `spend` description states 953.82 USD over 357
dispatches, measured 2026-08-14. The design's own re-based figures are 431 dispatches and 1254.26 USD. It
is **not** the deleted store's figure, so it fell outside the record that repaired those.

The deeper problem: `.basicly/usage/` is self ignored and worktree local, so **a published contract file
carries a number that no gate in this repository can re-derive**. A stale figure that cannot be checked
is worse than one that can, because nothing will ever notice it drift again - and this file is the
interface a foreign producer is told to conform to.

So the choice is to derive it, date it as a snapshot with its source named, or remove it from a contract
surface. This record does not choose.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the spend description in the board snapshot schema and note the figures and their date.
2. Read the design's re-based figures for the same quantities and observe they differ.
3. Attempt to re-derive the schema's figure from the repository and observe the usage directory is git ignored and worktree local.
4. Observe no gate reads the number, so nothing detects the drift.
5. Observe the file is the published contract a foreign producer conforms to.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a measurement stated in a published contract file then it is either derived by a gate or dated and attributed to a named source - check: `uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --check`
- Given the figure cannot be derived here then it is removed from the contract surface rather than left unverifiable

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`

## Working Set

- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest -q`
payload.title: the board schema publishes a spend measurement no gate in this repository can re-derive

payload.text:
Closed by 1617437b. Full verify PASS, 31 checks, 4501 tests. The acceptance check, docs_claims --check, passes; 42 board-schema tests hold.

The figure is off the contract surface, which is this record's second criterion, because the first was not available: proved that nothing under .basicly/usage/ is tracked by git, so no gate could ever re-derive it. The proof produced a THIRD number - the design says 431 dispatches, the schema said 357, this checkout holds 321. One quantity, three figures, none checkable.

The first criterion then sent me to look for other measurements on the same surface, and there were five more spans. Different case: the ledger IS tracked, so they are checkable, and they had drifted. The event log read 5890340 B against an actual 6396125 B, plus 8.6 percent in six days. The field-selection ratio moved 132.5x to 156.2x - stale in the direction that made the argument WEAKER than the truth. Re-derived, re-dated, and each now carries its previous reading so the next drift shows as a delta.

One correction of mine, and it is the same shape as the defect being fixed: my first count of active rows said 237 against the schema's 236, because I counted snapshot.jsonl's header line as a record. The schema was right and my instrument was wrong.

Not done, and it is the residual this record's own framing implies: a measurement in a tracked file can still go stale silently. The five figures I re-derived are dated, which the criterion accepts, but nothing derives them. docs_claims already has generated blocks for exactly this - a sixth block deriving the log size and the selection ratio would make the drift impossible rather than merely visible. That is not filed.

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-21 while recovering two lanes the spend bound stopped mid-flight. Both had committed-quality work staged and neither could commit:

```text
markdownlint............................................Failed
.basicly/usage/scratch/rn0o-3-plan.md:22 MD022/blanks-around-headings
.basicly/usage/scratch/rn0o-3-plan.md:23 MD032/blanks-around-lists
```

`.basicly/usage/.gitignore` holds `*`, so nothing under it is tracked or committable. The markdownlint hook globs `**/*.md !.venv/** !node_modules/**`, which reaches it anyway. A lane that writes itself a plan note - which the guidance encourages, and four of the five worktrees in this pass did - blocks every commit in its own worktree on a file that can never be committed.

One lane said so in its own transcript: *"I violated the scratch-file rule and it just bit me."* The rule it names is a prose rule; the gate is what actually fires, and it fires on the wrong population.

## Why this is the gate and not the lane

A machine-local, gitignored working file is not repository content. Linting it is the instrument reading outside its own population - the same class as counting a census file as part of its own census. The remedy is the glob, not more prose telling agents where to write.

Note the interaction with `basicly-jr0l.71`, which records a nested `node_modules` poisoning the same gate. Both are the same defect: the glob does not follow the ignore rules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the markdownlint hook runs, IT SHALL NOT lint a path git ignores.
- WHEN a lane writes a markdown note under `.basicly/usage/`, ITS COMMIT SHALL NOT be refused by markdownlint.
- WHEN a tracked markdown file breaks a rule, THE HOOK SHALL still refuse, and a test SHALL prove it on the same run that proves the exclusion.
- WHEN the hook reports its file count, THAT COUNT SHALL exclude the ignored paths, so the change is visible in the output rather than only in behaviour.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/markdownlint.py`
- `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
- `tests/test_hooks_markdownlint.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `70000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Write a deliberately malformed markdown file under `.basicly/usage/scratch/` and commit successfully, against a control malformed file at the repository root that the hook still refuses.

## Trigger

When basicly distributes Lefthook, I want every platform to use the pinned authoritative upstream artifact, so that consumers receive supported behavior without repository-owned binaries or a private fork.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run `git ls-files src/basicly/lefthook_assets` and inspect `src/basicly/lefthook_assets/manifest.json`; tracked Windows gzip executables and patch metadata are present, and preparation selects those custom artifacts instead of the official Windows release archives. - When hooks-build runs and a basicly-owned hook entry in a settings file names a script that does not exist, it shall remove that entry and report the removal.
- When hooks-check finds such an entry, it shall fail and name the entry and the script path.
- Hook entries that basicly does not own shall stay unchanged, and a test shall pin all three cases.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When a consumer moves between basicly releases, I want hooks-build to remove hook entries whose scripts it no longer ships, so I can run Bash without every call failing on a missing hook script.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install a newer basicly in a consumer, then discard the upgrade back to v0.12.2 with git reset --hard.
2. The gitignored .claude/settings.json keeps hook entries for rg-replace-guard.py and bare-var-guard.py; those scripts are absent in v0.12.2.
3. Every Bash call fails on the missing hook script, and hooks-build and hooks-check report up to date.

Reported 2026-10-07 by the burndown-chart session (burndownchart-xjl0x1); the owner removed the entries by hand. Related memory: projection is merge-never-prune.
payload.requirements:
- Never remove a hook entry the consumer wrote.
- Standard library only.
payload.title: hooks-build keeps a settings hook entry whose script is gone and reports up to date
